This cross-border collaboration promotes skills integration and the pooling of expertise in the semiconductor sector for defence.
By reducing dependence on non-European suppliers and democratizing military chip design, RESIST strengthens Europe’s industrial competitiveness and strategic autonomy in defense semiconductor manufacturing.

progetti.titolo: Sonobuoy Optimization for Unmanned Deployment and Underwater Detection
progetti.obiettivo:
The SOUND2 concept is designed to provide an UW surveillance solution based on sonobuoys deployment (i.e., a sonobuoys field) via multi-domain UxVs. The SOUND2 sonobuoy can be deployed and recovered from the unmanned platforms in unconventional scenarios to provide threat detection and classification capabilities in coastal waters, shallow waters, harbours, and offshore or subsea infrastructures. The SOUND2 system provides an integrated solution that enables cooperation between sonobuoys, unmanned vehicles and a centralized console, with a dedicated HMI to assist the end-user with optimising the system configuration, validating performance in a given scenario and monitoring operations in real-time during a mission. The console component can equip a control station installed on ground facilities, naval ships or airborne platform.
The SOUND2 project’s goal is to overcome the limitations of existing solutions, by developing an innovative approach to deploy & recovery, as well as cooperating with multi-domain UxVs and sonobuoys. Data gathered in the field can be processed, fused and analysed using novel and trustworthy AI-enabled algorithms, in order to detect, localise, track, recognise, and classify UW threat actors in proximity to a given surveillance perimeter. Operators can access system information via the console to gain 360° situational awareness, enabling them to monitor unfolding scenarios and remain alert to emerging threats.
In brief, SOUND2 enables both a rapid response capability in regions that typically lack adequate surveillance systems and an enhanced deterrence posture in the event of a heightened threat level. Furthermore, SOUND2 can be used to extend the ASW capabilities of EU Navies. Indeed, SOUND2 provides a flexible and cost-efficient solution for the deployment and use of sonobuoys in ASW operations, by replacing helicopters or MPAs with smaller unmanned vehicles that can be hosted on board a vessel.

progetti.titolo: Multilayer anti-jam protection for GNSS receivers
progetti.obiettivo:
Despite being specifically designed to combat relatively high-power radio interference, GNSS systems are today subject to a large number of possible radio operation threats. In fact, due to its open nature, this route is the main tool used by attackers interested in causing the disruption of the GNSS service of receivers of specific systems or of all receivers located in a certain geographical area. Intentional attacks on GNSS systems usually aim at the degradation or complete interruption of the service (jamming attack), or, in rarer cases, the falsification of service signals (spoofing attack) to cause a erroneous calculation of the position or time of the attacked receiver.
In addition, GNSS receivers are subject to a variety of unintentional electromagnetic interference in different frequency bands caused by external systems or by the same system where the receiver is installed.
The general objective of the GNSS-ARMOUR consortium is to carry out, the design, prototyping and testing of a new comprehensive solution for shielding GNSS receivers, intended to become in the short term the most complete, usable and best-performing solution available on the market. In particular:
• GNSS-ARMOUR will use, in a same device, state-of-the-art protection methods at the antenna level, digital baseband and GNSS processing, and will seek their optimal combination through real-time coordination
• GNSS-ARMOUR will provide a complete shielded GNSS solution, including a custom-designed antenna and software-defined GNSS receiver; and at the same time will provide a clean GNSS signal
• GNSS-ARMOUR will enable appropriate monitoring and control interfaces to allow optimal deployment, configuration, integration and operation within the system where the solution is installed
• GNSS-ARMOUR will be validated on preoperational Defence scenarios with Unmanned Ground and Aerial vehicles
• GNSS-ARMOUR is designed as interoperable solution, that can work with any GNSS receiver

progetti.titolo: Neuromorphic Event-Driven Vision for Multiple Defense Applications
progetti.obiettivo:
Modern defence platforms face growing challenges in maintaining situational awareness and autonomy under contested conditions. Drone swarms, high-speed munitions, and asymmetric tactics have revealed the limits of conventional radar and optical systems, which suffer from latency, poor low-light performance, and vulnerability to electronic warfare. Simultaneously, GNSS denial undermines autonomous navigation, while covert surveillance in darkness or cluttered terrain remains difficult.
The NEVMA project develops and validates a neuromorphic event-driven vision system designed for modern defence operations. Integrating event-based cameras, infrared sensors, and spiking neural networks within a compact hardware–software framework, it enables millisecond-scale motion detection, onboard classification and trajectory prediction, and GNSS-independent navigation. NEVMA delivers a flexible perception layer applicable to air defence, ground operations, and maritime surveillance.
Its innovations focus on three domains: (i) High-speed threat detection and classification, merging neuromorphic vision with traditional and IR cameras fusion for early warning and accurate trajectory prediction of aerial or surface threats. (ii) Autonomous navigation in GNSS-denied environments, using event-driven SLAM and landmark detection to ensure obstacle avoidance and localisation for UGVs. (iii) Low-light and obscured-environment surveillance, combining neuromorphic and infrared sensing for covert ISR missions.
Advancing from TRL 4 to TRL 7, NEVMA will deliver integrated prototypes validated in near-operational scenarios such as UAV interception, GNSS-free navigation, and coastal surveillance. By leveraging European sensor and AI technologies, NEVMA reinforces European Defence Technological and Industrial Base (EDTIB) capabilities, supports SME innovation in embedded vision and defence electronics, and enables dual-use applications in border security and critical infrastructure monitoring.

progetti.titolo: 5G NTN FOR EUROPEAN DEFENCE OPERATIONS
progetti.obiettivo:
5G4Def delivers a standards-native 5G Non-Terrestrial Network capability tailored to defence “big-pipe” missions that demand very-high throughput, reliability, and security. Unlike direct-to-device initiatives, 5G4Def targets gigabit-class broadband per terminal using parabolic or flat-panel antennas, enabling resilient C2, ISR video, and multi-domain operations in contested electromagnetic environments. The solution is built on open interfaces—3GPP 5G-NTN and DIFI—and integrates a software-defined modem family (UE, gNB, DVB-S2X) that runs across heterogeneous hardware, from COTS gateways to flight-qualified payload compute. A hardened real-time platform, Osmium OS, provides secure/verified boot, signed updates, remote attestation, and deterministic performance.

Two use cases structure the work: UC1 (Secure GEO Ground Terminal) establishes a deployable 5G NTN “bubble” that backhauls over DVB-S2X or 5G-native gateway links; UC2 (Regenerative LEO Payload) brings GPU-accelerated on-board 5G RAN to terminate NR-NTN in space, cutting latency and unlocking dynamic resource allocation, interference mitigation, and slice-aware routing. 

The programme strengthens the European Defence Technological and Industrial Base (EDTIB) and security of supply by anchoring design authority, IP, and manufacturing in Europe, and by creating a modular, multi-vendor chain: NXGSAT (UE/gNB + DVB-S2X), Unibap (on-board GPU compute), Integrasys (DIFI digitizer + channel emulator), and Osmium (secure RT OS). Open interfaces enable second-source EU suppliers and prevent lock-in; Lifecycle efficiency improves through COTS hardware, software-defined upgrades, automation , and “test once, field many” with a high-fidelity channel emulator.

Aligned with IRIS² goals, 5G4Def provides a scalable, interoperable, and sovereign European 5G-NTN backbone—ready to progress to TRL7 (GEO) and TRL6 (LEO) and to underpin future defence connectivity programmes.

progetti.titolo: LIGHTWEIGHT SECURE COMMUNICATION PROTOCOL WITH HW-BACKED POST-QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY
progetti.obiettivo:
SEQULITE is a European‐designed, certified VPN that forms a “secure hose” between any two endpoints. It does not matter if the link hops via LEO satellites, GEO relays, or public cellular backhauls – the encrypted and authenticated tunnel never breaks as long as some connectivity exists. SEQULITE’s features include: I) End-to-End, Quantum-Resistant Encryption, supporting hybrid-mode operation: All traffic (any IP data) is encrypted with EU-approved algorithms that are quantum-safe; II) Sovereign Key Management: Cryptographic keys and sensitive operations are held either in EU-made tamper-resistant HW or in a lightweight EU-developed SW library; III) Certifiable Assurance: Common Criteria certification under the new EUCC scheme means that defence procurement agencies can trust it in acquisition and field use. The consortium intends to invest heavily in certification to ensure SEQULITE is not only innovative but truly market‑ready.
It works in two complementary forms: a) as a sealed HW/SW communication module with a HW root of trust, based on an FPGA-implemented HSM. This version is intended for platforms that require tamper resistance, key isolation, and physical assurance; b) a lightweight SW library that embeds the same secure tunnel into existing high-security modems or terminals, for cases where HW add-ons are impractical.

Each participant contributes a distinct and essential capability: OSMIUM and SKUDO form the core technical team, covering SW(protocol) and HW cryptography. ARGOTEC supports on orbital specificities for the protocol design and together with DSIS and MILTECH provide real-world deployment contexts and testing environments. TAMCERT guarantees the certification of SEQULITE components.

SEQULITE boosts EU defence autonomy by closing gaps in the Strategic Compass and EU defence priorities in cyber and secure comm. It secures supply chains, reduces foreign tech reliance, and supports EDTIB through sovereign solutions and strategic partnerships.

progetti.titolo: Robust privacy-preserving adaptive Human-AI dialoguE System for trustworthy and explaInable defence applicationS
progetti.bando: Privacy-preserving human-AI dialogue systems – Participation in a technological challenge
progetti.obiettivo: RHESIS aims to develop a transformative defence-oriented human-AI dialogue system able to interact with end-users in writing and by voice in all official EU languages in the context of diverse defence applications, such as intelligence, strategic planning, tactical operations, and life-cycle support. RHESIS will perform defence domain adaptation of an existing EU Large Language Model (LLM), through advanced techniques for AI model customisation in order to immerse the model in the target domain’s language and knowledge patterns, and subsequent fine-tuning to specific defence dialogue scenarios. To properly handle sensitive/classified information, RHESIS will enforce privacy preservation by providing user-specific outputs on a need-to-know basis and will also accompany the generated outputs with human-understandable explanations. To contextualise the generated outputs to particular users, RHESIS will integrate a continuously learning component that allows the system to learn from its interactions with end-users. The developed human-AI dialogue system will be designed to be robust to different types of attacks, while also ensuring its trustworthiness and fairness through reducing bias. RHESIS will efficiently integrate all aforementioned AI modules into a defence-oriented human-AI dialogue system demonstrator with a user-friendly interface. The developed system will be evaluated through RHESIS’ participation in evaluation campaigns organised by the project to be funded under EDF-2025-LS-RA-CHALLENGE-DIGIT-HAIDO. To assist the evaluation process, RHESIS will contribute by developing complementary AI-based correction systems. Finally, RHESIS will ensure legal and ethical compliance of the developed AI solutions, in alignment with EU legislation/regulations. With a strong consortium of 12 partners (8 SMEs/ Mid-Caps, 3 RTOs, and 1 large industry) from 7 countries, RHESIS delivers a strong representation of the challenges, requirements, and tools to meet its objectives.

progetti.titolo: Secure, Human-AI, Interactive, Edge, Language, Dialogue
progetti.bando: Privacy-preserving human-AI dialogue systems – Participation in a technological challenge
progetti.obiettivo:
Modern military operations demand real-time, multilingual and secure decision support in environments where connectivity is limited and information is sensitive. The operators must interpret and address complex, fast-evolving data to make real-time, informed decisions — often without access to cloud-based tools or external networks. In such conditions, the AI-SHIELD proposes a private, deployable, sustainable and efficient large language model (LLM) becoming a strategic asset for the end-users. The project's solution enables enhanced intelligence analysis, situational awareness, mission planning, resource management and tactical decision support without compromisingthe  data confidentiality and the operational autonomy.
The system builds upon open-source European LLMs from the OpenEuroLLM initiative and introduces a disruptive innovation through quantum-inspired model compression technology that reduces model size and energy consumption by up to 80% with minimal loss in performance. This enables the deployment of advanced generative AI on edge devices and secure on-premise systems, ensuring low latency, reduced computational footprint, reduced costs and full operational control. AI-SHIELD is one of four participating projects in the challenge. The challenge is organized by the consortium dedicated to the challenge set-up.

progetti.titolo: Middleware for Intelligent Defense AI Dialogue Systems
progetti.bando: Privacy-preserving human-AI dialogue systems – Participation in a technological challenge
progetti.obiettivo:
The MIDAS project addresses a pressing challenge in the European defence landscape: the need for rapid, accurate, and secure synthesis of vast and diverse information to support high-stakes operational decisions. In today’s complex mission environments, the speed and effectiveness of military responses rely heavily on the ability to collect, interpret, and act upon large volumes of structured and unstructured data. However, this demand often collides with real-world constraints such as limited personnel availability, compressed decision windows, and the risk of cognitive overload and human error. To resolve these challenges, MIDAS proposes a novel concept: the development of a secure, explainable, and modular AI middleware platform designed specifically for defence applications. The platform integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) and intelligent AI agents to facilitate real-time, role-aware dialogue and decision support across strategic, tactical, and operational layers. The system builds upon key innovations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), explainable AI, secure human-AI interfaces, and cyber defence mechanisms, enabling seamless human-machine teaming even in air-gapped, multilingual, and resource-constrained military environments. With built-in explainability, access control, and legal-ethical compliance, the MIDAS platform is engineered to meet the stringent standards of trust, transparency, and interoperability required by EU armed forces.
By uniting leading organizations with deep expertise in defence-grade technologies, the MIDAS project aims not only to demonstrate the feasibility of deploying LLMs in defence, but to establish them as an operational capability aligned with the principles of the EU AI Act, GDPR, and other defence regulatory frameworks, thereby reinforcing European sovereignty in the realm of advanced technologies.
In essence, MIDAS transforms LLMs from experimental tools into mission-ready enablers.

progetti.titolo: Sovereign and trusted large language models for European defence and security
progetti.bando: Privacy-preserving human-AI dialogue systems – Participation in a technological challenge
progetti.obiettivo:
LLM SECRET is one of four selected projects participating in this EDF technological challenge, coordinated through an organiser project to accelerate trusted defence AI capabilities in Europe. Modern defence operations generate vast flows of information; the real challenge is trust. LLM SECRET delivers the first sovereign European dialogue system based on large language models (LLMs), designed for classified and offline use. It combines zero-trust security, explainable reasoning, and edge-grade deployment to provide reliable AI support in contested environments.
The project tackles five critical challenges: explainability under stress, decision speed under data overload, insider threats, resilience to deception, and continuity in disconnected theatres. Four operational use cases (maintenance, OSINT in northern regions, forensic analysis, and feedback from military drone exercises) will validate performance across tactical, analytical, and strategic domains.
Within 48 months, LLM SECRET will deliver a sovereign AI demonstrator, reinforcing Europe’s capability priorities in C4ISTAR, Cyber Defence, and Future Soldier Systems; a concrete step toward trusted cognitive superiority.

progetti.titolo: Advanced Breakthrough sYstems for SubSea Autonomy
progetti.obiettivo:
ABYSSA is an innovative research project aimed at advancing disruptive technologies for safe, resilient and sustainable operations in the deep-sea environment. It focuses on the development of autonomous and high-performance underwater systems capable of operating at depths of up to 6000 metres, addressing key challenges related to energy supply, navigation, sensing, communication and long-term operation under extreme conditions. Critical underwater infrastructures, such as communication cables, energy pipelines and offshore installations, are essential to modern society but face increasing environmental and operational challenges. ABYSSA aims to enhance the monitoring, inspection and protection of these assets through intelligent underwater systems capable of continuous observation, data collection and anomaly detection.

The project brings together a multidisciplinary consortium of industry, research organisations, SMEs and universities from across Europe to explore and integrate advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, digital twins, next-generation sensing systems and innovative materials. These technologies will be studied, designed and validated through simulations and controlled testing environments, contributing to future underwater solutions. By combining expertise from multiple sectors, ABYSSA strengthens European defence and technological capabilities in the underwater domain by enabling persistent surveillance, protection, and autonomous operation around critical underwater infrastructure in hostile maritime environments; while generating knowledge with applications in environmental monitoring, marine research and offshore energy.

progetti.titolo: Disruptive Underwater Technology Capability Enabler for EU Next-Generation Deep-Sea Operations and Autonomous Subsea Technologies
progetti.obiettivo: DEEP-TECH is a disruptive technology enabler concept designed to drive the knowledge, studies, and design of the next-generation EU defence subsea technologies. Enhancing surveillance, protection methodologies and approaches, extending the operational range, capabilities and autonomy of unmanned systems in high-depth and extreme maritime environments and developing the next generation of resident and autonomous unmanned systems for seabed warfare. Focused on pushing the limits of deep-sea SBW operations, DEEP-TECH facilitates the creation of breakthrough capabilities for AUVs, ROVs, Relocatable and robotic Seabed Landers nodes, and autonomous underwater infrastructures and base stations, to establish a resident autonomous surveillance and protection system that can scale to wide areas, cover the full water column, and address all European seas (Atlantic, Mediteranea, Baltic, Arctic, ...). Integrating advancements in docking, energy storage and wireless transfer, communication, autonomous detection and neutralisation of incoming threats, and sensor networks to enhance persistence, resilience, and unmanned systems capabilities in high-risk, high-depth scenarios, and be able to protect against the current and future threats using large and long-range autonomous vehicles.

progetti.titolo: Spin-based neural networks for RF processing and learning at the edge
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions targeting disruptive technologies for defence
progetti.obiettivo:
Spin Defender proposes a radically new way to process RF signals. It substitutes digitization by spin-based learning, providing massive advantages for defence operations: large instantaneous bandwidth (10 MHz – 50 GHz), small size (mm2 chip), high speed (μs per computation), low power consumption (1 W) and adaptability to changing environments.
In Spin Defender, digitization-free spectrum analysis and advanced AI processing are performed directly in hardware using arrays of spintronic nanodevices.

The EU is currently at the international forefront of the development and fabrication of this type of nanodevices and today, thanks to our advanced understanding of their physics and our fabrication expertise, we are ready to create a prototype system that demonstrates the disruptive potential of this technology for RF signal processing.

Spin Defender technology brings disruptive advantages for electronic warfare, signal intelligence and radar systems: wide bandwidth, fast processing, low power and compact chip, adaptability and versatility through learning. 

In Spin Defender we will perform a TRL 4 proof of concept of RF AI chip on a Signal Intelligence use case. Furthermore, we will establish a 100 % EU sovereign supply chain to ensure full EDTIP autonomy.

progetti.titolo: European Unified Aerial Security Ecosystem - Systemic Protection and Escalation Control for Threat Response in Europe
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions targeting disruptive technologies for defence
progetti.obiettivo:
The SPECTRE project delivers a disruptive, modular, and legally grounded System-of-Systems (SoS) architecture to counter the rising threat of small unmanned aerial systems (sUAS) across national and cross-border European defence environments. SPECTRE elevates the concept to the European level by combining technology, doctrine, and legal governance into one scalable, interoperable solution.
SPECTRE develops a next-generation hybrid system that integrates advanced Unmanned Traffic Management (UTM) technology and Counter - Unmanned Aerial System (C-UAS) information sharing into a self-learning, autonomous digital ecosystem, enabling radically superior defence control over drone operations in multi-domain and sensitive areas across various environments, including high-threat regions. Through open interface specifications, GDPR-compliant legal logic, and adaptive threat response protocols, SPECTRE enables fast deployment in both civil and defence environments. 
Central to SPECTRE is its replacement of the static concept-of-operations (CONOPS) with a reusable Framework Development Document (FDD) tailored for cross-sector deployment and NATO/EU mission integration.
Led by a multinational consortium of defence integrators, researchers, operational end-users and legal experts, SPECTRE bridges the gap between standalone C-UAS technologies and fully integrated, ethically deployable European capabilities. Its dual-use applicability, modular architecture, and open standards approach ensure both strategic relevance and commercial sustainability.

progetti.titolo: Concatenated Parity codes on Neutral Atoms
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions targeting disruptive technologies for defence
progetti.obiettivo:
The objectives of CoPaNA are twofold. First, it proposes to lay the scientific foundation for building the next generation quantum computer. To do so, CoPaNA focuses on the development of new scientific methods to make quantum computers more stable and scalable, a necessary pre-requisite for unlocking their full disruptive potential and added value to the economy and society. 
Second, by focusing on error-correction, fault-tolerant quantum computing and advanced neutral-atom-based technologies, CoPaNA also aims to lay the industrial foundations for computational breakthroughs and concrete use case application developments in the defense sector such as battlefield applications, enhanced algorithmic optimisation, simulation for material development, quantum sensing and detection, intelligence, cryptography and mission planning.
The consortium—comprising SME ParityQC, large company THALES, and mid-cap Pasqal (CoPaNa’s Coordinator)—combines expertise in neutral atom quantum hardware, quantum architectures and algorithms, error correction, and high-tech defence solutions to achieve computational power beyond classical systems.
Aligned with the 2023 EU Capability Development Priorities, the white paper for European Defence and the ReArm Europe Plan- Readiness 2030, the 2025 EU Quantum Strategy and the European Economic Security Strategy, CoPaNA will reinforce Europe’s resilience, technological sovereignty and its European Defence Technological Industrial Base by developing new dual-use quantum applications for the defence sector. It advances the mid-term vision of secure, interoperable, and sovereign access to next-generation quantum computing capabilities for Europe while giving the opportunity to European Armed Forces to get equipped with the latest quantum applications to make both their operations more efficient and strategic to solve the most pressing 21st century global defense challenges.

progetti.titolo: Soldier Operational Autonomous Resilient Energy System
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions targeting disruptive technologies for defence
progetti.obiettivo: SOLARES proposes a disruptive new approach to energy and power on-field operations by introducing a fully autonomous, water-propelled hydrogen ecosystem powered by renewable electricity. To support true independence, SOLARES integrates a Deployable Tactical Hydrogen Supply (DTHS), a portable solar- and wind-powered refilling unit that generates, compresses, and recharges cartridges directly in the field with minimal noise and signature, removing dependence on convoys or base resupply. Hydrogen will power a lightweight wearable PEM fuel cell system with advanced modular hydrogen cartridges and a small battery/supercapacitor buffer, capable of providing 50W continuously for over 72 hours. This represents a significant increase in capacity compared to current batteries, reducing carried weight by up to 70% and enabling soldiers to operate longer, safer, and with high-power devices such as advanced communications, sensors, and UAVs.  The cartridges themselves, developed with lightweight composites are robust, safe, and potentially conformal to the soldier’s body, while their modular design enables fast swapping and multi-domain use. Crucially, the same cartridge standard can be applied across UAVs, UGVs, robotics, field hospitals, disaster relief systems, and renewable microgrids, transforming energy logistics into a flexible, scalable and dual-use framework. By combining multiphysics simulations, abusive testing and ergonomic modelling, SOLARES goes beyond incremental improvements and offers a clean, emission-free energy ecosystem. The project enhances autonomy, survivability, and operational flexibility of European forces, while reducing reliance on non-EU battery and methanol technologies, and opening new dual-use markets in defence, mobility, and civil resilience.

progetti.titolo: eNabling EXTended SWIR imaging
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions targeting disruptive technologies for defence
progetti.obiettivo:
The NEXTSWIR project aims to develop highly sensitive HgCdTe avalanche photodiodes (APD) and lasers for active and passive remote sensing in the eSWIR band. This band can provide advantages for long-range target discrimination compared to the standard visible, NIR, SWIR, and MWIR bands due to a better balance of transmission and diffraction limit. However, its application has been challenging due to the scarcity of photons.
NEXTSWIR will demonstrate the benefits of HgCdTe APD technology in the eSWIR band for ground (long-range observation) and space (early warning) applications, by developing a high sensitivity, low noise and high acquisition rate imaging technology in the eSWIR band based on HgCdTe APD as well as developing a 2μm laser. Several scenarios are envisioned, for passive and active imaging, in continuous and gated modes.
The ENEXSWIR project involves 10 partners from 4 European countries, including RTOs, SMEs, and LEs, covering the entire value chain from specifications to technological development, integration, and applications.

progetti.titolo: STRATUS – Swarm Threat Resilience and Adaptive Tactical UxV Security
progetti.bando: Risk, robustness and resilience for autonomous vehicles in military operations
progetti.obiettivo: The future battlespace is increasingly defined by digital interconnectivity, data fusion, and autonomous decision-making. Modern military operations are evolving into fully digital, multi-domain environments where land, air, maritime, space, and cyber assets operate as tightly coupled, sensor-rich, and AI-enabled systems. Unmanned vehicles (UxVs) – including drones, ground robots, and autonomous maritime platforms – are central to this transformation, providing expanded reach, precision, and reduced risk to personnel. However, this cyber-physical integration creates new systemic vulnerabilities. A single compromise in swarm coordination logic, communication links, or autonomy software can cascade across an entire force, disrupting operations or even turning UxVs into hostile assets. The operational environment itself becomes part of the attack surface, as adversaries manipulate sensors, electromagnetic emissions, or environmental cues to deceive AI-driven systems. Traditional cybersecurity architectures, designed for static, enterprise IT systems, are inadequate for the dynamic, adversarial, and latency-sensitive conditions of military operations. UxVs rely on distributed edge processing, contested communication links, and often commercial supply-chain components – each a potential for exploitation. Future conflicts will involve persistent cyber fires, cognitive electronic warfare, and information deception across the electromagnetic spectrum. In this environment, resilience – not mere protection – becomes the defining characteristic of credible autonomy. STRATUS directly confronts this urgent reality with a bold solution: a multi-layered, AI-driven, risk-based cyber defence system that enables autonomous UxV swarms to survive, adapt, and complete their missions under attack. This high-level initiative creates a new standard of resilience and innovation, ensuring that UxVs remain trusted force multipliers even in contested cyber-electromagnetic environments.

progetti.titolo: Modular Integration of Naval Energy Systems for Resilient Vessels Application
progetti.bando: Naval hybrid propulsion and power systems
progetti.obiettivo:
Transitioning the European naval fleet from reliance on fossil fuels to the adoption of renewable energy sources is a critical step for European strategic autonomy, both in order to meet the targets for the European green deal and to reduce the reliance on Russian and other nations resources. At the same time, the military performance of the Naval fleet needs to be improved in order to meet higher energy demands of mission systems and hybrid propulsion systems and to be able to operate in contested environments. In the civilian sector, the development and implementation of alternative energy sources and DC electrical power systems is already well underway. However, adapting these solutions for military use presents unique challenges due to the specific and demanding requirements of defence operations. Special attention and tailored approaches are therefore needed to ensure that renewable energy technologies can meet the demanding standards of military applications.
MINERVA – Modular Integration of Naval Energy Systems for Resilient Vessels Application – will respond to this challenge by accelerating the design process for energy systems of naval vessels with a modular and hybrid propulsion and hybrid DC power system architecture and a novel modelling, simulation and testing approach for improving military performance of naval vessels. Based on numerous innovative technologies developed for civilian applications, MINERVA will adopt three key innovation areas for military use: fuel-flexible hybrid propulsion systems, DC electric power systems and energy storage and a joint modular Design, Modelling and Test Approach. The project will demonstrate the new set-up in a holistic virtual environment combining distributed physical test facilities with a joint virtual modelling and simulation environment with advanced and AI-based digital twins. The consortium brings together 20 beneficiaries, consisting of major European shipyards, OEMs, research organisations and SMEs.

progetti.titolo: TACTICAL-CAPTURE: DEVELOPMENT OF TACTICALLY RESPONSIVE IN-SPACE MOBILITY AND STANDARD INTERFACE-LESS CAPTURE TECHNOLOGY BY WELDING
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
Space assets are vital for Europe’s civil and defence operations but remain increasingly exposed to hostile actions such as satellite shadowing, jamming, and potential asset denial. TAC project addresses this strategic vulnerability by developing a tactically responsive servicer capable of inspecting, capturing, and attaching to any spacecraft - prepared or unprepared - using a welding-based capture process. Unlike conventional docking systems requiring standardized interfaces and extreme precision, welding enables secure attachment through controlled contact, reducing AOCS complexity and cost while increasing mission flexibility and responsiveness.
TAC will advance three technological pillars to TRL 5: (1) a robotic electron-beam welding process with in-situ diagnostics for weld quality control; (2) adaptive GNC and contact dynamics algorithms enabling synchronization and compliant contact with tumbling or uncooperative targets; and (3) an integrated servicer architecture validated through a digital twin up to Preliminary Design Review.
This combination enables new mission classes—asset protection, relocation, deorbiting, and modular attachment—addressing clear gaps in Europe’s tactical space capabilities. The same welding process also supports module integration (life extension, SSA sensors, deorbit kits), bridging civil and military uses and proving the dual-use and cost-efficient nature of the investment.
TAC directly contributes to European defence capability priorities in space resilience, deterrence, and situational awareness, aligning with the Capability Development Plan, Strategic Compass, and CFSP objectives. By maturing a reusable, sovereign, and modular servicer, TAC strengthens Europe’s autonomy and industrial base in a domain dominated by non-EU actors, positioning it to act decisively in a contested and congested space environment.

progetti.titolo: Fused Analytics and Smart Textiles for real-time operational readiness in soldier TRAINing
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
FAST-TRAIN turbocharges European defence training with a new, sovereign “humanstate” sensing layer. FAST-TRAIN will fuse miniaturised brain and body signals (helmetcompatible fNIRS, washable ICG electrodes, and textileintegrated IMUs) with secure, onbody edge AI to turn raw data into live cognitive and physiological scores, all with no cloud dependence. The result: adaptive, safer, faster learning cycles in realistic simulators and fieldlike drills. 

Our EU SME–RO powerhouse will design defencegrade smart garments and a cap that fit under standard kit, survive 100+ wash cycles, and deliver missionrelevant insights without getting in the way. By spinning in proven civil tech and pushing it to defence ruggedness, FAST-TRAIN aims to cut timetoproficiency, lift skill acquisition, and reduce attrition in highcost pipelines, while protecting privacy. Entirely European in supply and knowhow, the project strengthens EDTIB autonomy and lays the foundation for nextgen LVC training, selection, and humanmachine teaming. Real training. Real signals. Realtime readiness.

progetti.titolo: Disruptive Materials for Submarine Invisibility.
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
The main object of PRIORITY is to develop advanced materials with extreme capacities for a full reduction of the acoustic and magnetic signature of submarines. The key concept to produce extreme isolation and extreme anechoic capacity at macroscopic level is a new paradigm in the microscopic material design based on the programming of gradients into the base foams, the incorporation of chemical treatments, additives or viscoaerogels to exploit the intermolecular forces and interactions between the solid skeleton.
These materials have extraordinary capabilities that can significantly diminish the acoustic footprint of submarines to a mere one millionth of what is achievable with conventional materials. Additionally, the multifunctional nature of these materials will impart antifouling and super hydrophobic properties, thereby mitigating drag forces. These advance high-performance foams promise a remarkable 95% reduction in weight compared to traditional elastomeric materials, enhancing submarine manoeuvrability. This is attributed to the isochoric behaviours of open-cell foams saturated by seawater during dives, where their volume remains insensitive to the immersion level.
The pioneering technology of PRIORITY modifies the intermolecular forces and viscous damping of materials, leading to a significant modification of wave propagation velocity and acoustic dissipation.
Besides, a 3D computational virtual laboratory, together with the experimental laboratories for materials, will be fundamental to achieve the validation of the technology in real submarine acoustic problems. The achievement of this objective involves the development of a computational platform that combines Finite Element Technology and Boundary Element Technologies. This platform should be capable of modelling the acoustic interaction between solid and porous media saturated with air, water, gels, or viscous aerogels, as well as the interaction of different porous media.

progetti.titolo: Unmanned Heavy-lift Aerial Reconnaissance and Resilient Integrated European Response
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
U-HARRIER (Unmanned Heavy-lift Aerial Reconnaissance and Resilient Integrated European Response) will design, develop and validate an innovative heavy-lift Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) able to transport up to 300 kg of supplies in contested, GNSS-denied or degraded environments. The system addresses critical gaps in European defence logistics and reconnaissance by combining high payload capacity, low observability, autonomy, and rapid field repairability within a modular and interoperable platform.
U-HARRIER introduces disruptive technologies: lightweight composite ballistic protection, multispectral camouflage and EMI shielding, AI-driven Structural Health Monitoring with in-field repair kits, Digital Twin-based predictive maintenance, immersive AR/VR tools for operator training, and secure swarm flight control with quantum-resistant communications. These advances will deliver a stealth-enabled, cyber-resilient UAV capable of operating collaboratively in swarm formations and integrating seamlessly with NATO/EU logistics standards.
The 36-month project, implemented by nine partners from six EU Member States (SMEs and RTOs), will reach TRL 6, producing a validated system concept that strengthens Europe’s strategic autonomy, resilience, and technological sovereignty in aerial logistics. Beyond defence, the results will open dual-use applications in civil protection, humanitarian aid and disaster relief, reinforcing the European Defence Technological and Industrial Base (EDTIB) and fostering sustainable SME growth within the EU supply chain.

progetti.titolo: Next Generation Modular AI-driven live augmented Training System
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
MANTIS (Next Generation Modular AI-driven Live-Augmented Training System) develops a European, modular capability for realistic, adaptive tactical training that fuses XR lenses/helmets, a haptic textile suit (“MANTIS Skin”), a sensorised TCCC/IFAK toolkit, and a laser-based weapon simulation (LWS) with an AI-enabled, portable C2 Tactical Training Station. The C2 is architected as a rugged, high-performance CPU edge platform (containerised services, deterministic low-latency pipelines) protected by a Zero-Trust Architecture (ZTA) for identity, authentication, authorisation, and encrypted communications across all subsystems. This approach ensures deployability in disconnected/contested environments, security-by-design, and alignment with EU technological-sovereignty goals.

The overall ambition is to redefine tactical training in Europe by providing an adaptive, interoperable, and secure platform that prepares forces for the increasing complexity, uncertainty, and hybrid nature of modern operations.

Objectives and scope. MANTIS will (i) specify a human-centred, interoperable architecture for live-augmented training; (ii) prototype key subsystems (XR optics, haptic textiles, sensorised IFAK) and their interfaces; (iii) implement AI services for adaptive orchestration, monitoring and evaluation; and (iv) deliver a portable C2 tactical trainer ready for field deployment in controlled trials. Activities are strictly research and design with lab-scale validation: the consortium will mature technologies up to TRL-4 (functional validation in laboratory/controlled settings), consistent with EDF Research Actions (“low TRL—up to ~4/5”); MANTIS commits to not exceeding TRL-4 within this action.

progetti.titolo: Electro Magnetic Modular Ordnance for Rapid Tactical Artillery Response
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo: The EM-MORTAR project proposes a feasibility study and conceptual design for an electromagnetic mortar launcher capable of replacing traditional chemical propellants with pulsed electromagnetic acceleration. This innovative concept will deliver silent operation and adjustable muzzle velocity with extreme precision, two features that provide decisive tactical advantages in modern warfare—particularly in close-combat and urban environments where traditional mortars expose their positions through loud acoustic and visual signatures.

progetti.titolo: Towards Robust 3D printed metallic components production for military applications by the development of innovative SURface FINishing and design protocols
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
Metal Additive Manufacturing has emerged as a transformative technology in the military industry, offering flexibility to produce functional parts on-demand and on-site. Despite its potential, AM faces significant challenges, particularly in postprocessing, which is crucial for achieving the desired final properties and tolerances of printed parts.
Current post-processing methods are costly, complex, and not always suitable for deployment in military missions. Heat treatment and machining are well-established processes and may be implemented in warships and military camps. However, it is not the case of support removal and surface finishing, which implies, apart from machining, polishing and surface functionalisation.
The project addresses these challenges by developing innovative post-processing solutions tailored for military applications for parts made by Powder Bed Fusion (PBF) and wire-Direct Energy deposition (DED), introducing cutting-edge technologies:
• vibration-based support removal system, dry suspension and gel-based electrolyte surface finishing, for PBF parts
• dry-suspension electrolyte surface finishing applied by projection and gel-based passivation, for DED parts
These technologies are designed to be easy implemented in military missions, addressing the unique needs of defense applications.
They are also suitable for being used by military industry producing AM parts and may be used for civil applications. In addition, R3DSURFIN will provide: 
1) Design wizard to optimise the PBF manufacturing, considering postprocessing constraints; 
2) Surface roughness predictive module to optimise the surface characteristics of as-built DED parts; and 
3) Predictive models to simulate surface treatments with dry-suspension and gel electrolytes.
6 different EU countries are participating, and the consortium is formed and led by 4 SMEs, whose involvement is crucial for driving R3DSURFIN solution towards successful exploitation, opening new market opportunities.

progetti.titolo: Autonomous Expeditionary Guardian and Interceptor Swarm through distributed Networked Engagement Technology
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo: AEGIS-NET proposes the design of a cost-effective, mobile, autonomous, GNSS-independent and Electronic Warfare (EW)-tolerant, purpose-built, short-range air defence (SHORAD) system, for tactical C-UAS operations, to protect forward elements and frontline units that are vulnerable and highly exposed to loitering munition attacks, thereby offloading the burden of manual threat engagement and enhancing operational resilience. AEGIS-NET integrates vehicle-mounted nodes and attritable fibre-optic tethered rocket-shaped UAV Interceptors, with human-on-the-loop control.  AEGIS-NET delivers sensor fusion of multi-parametric passive sensing (EO, acoustic, RF/ESM, RGBD) for rapid detection, tracking and identification and threat classification; intent prediction and intercept geometry; MARL-based swarm coordination; PNT-resilient navigation and comms; auditable engagement logic; and a mobile docking station for launch, recharge and rearm to sustain magazine depth. Validation uses digital twins and hardware-in-the-loop to reach Critical Design Definition through iterative Test Cases: i) Perimeter defence of forward units under coordinated swarms; ii) Convoy protection in open terrain under GNSS denial/EW; and iii) Selective, low-collateral response in congested airspace with friendly UAVs. AEGIS-NET strengthens European strategic autonomy by delivering an indigenous, ITAR-free, interoperable C-UAS/SHORAD layer aligned with EU CDP priorities, reducing foreign dependencies and reinforcing the EDTIB through SME-led innovation and scalable supply chains.

progetti.titolo: High-temperature resistant and durable multispectral camouflage system
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
Modern multispectral camouflage textiles must provide concealment across the visible, infrared, and radar spectrum to counter advanced surveillance systems. Conventional solutions such as printed patterns or metallic coatings deliver partial protection but remain limited by poor durability, thermal instability, glare, and lack of adaptability. Many current fabrics rely on polyester or nylon, which deform or melt at moderate heat, and their functional coatings often lose effectiveness after exposure to harsh environments, flexing, or washing.

ResistCAM addresses these shortcomings by developing a new class of composite textiles that combine high-temperature resistant substrates with multifunctional nanofiber membranes and advanced coatings. The concept is based on a hierarchically layered structure: an outer metallized or graphene-based surface with low emissivity, a porous nanofiber interlayer that insulates and equalizes heat flow, and inner supporting fabrics that provide mechanical robustness and user comfort. The nanofiber core acts as a thermal sponge, reducing hotspots and suppressing infrared signatures while remaining lightweight and breathable.

The project will integrate three classes of functional materials. Metals such as silver or nickel deliver very low emissivity and strong radar scattering. Graphene provides high thermal conductivity, distributing heat laterally while contributing electrical conductivity and shielding. MXenes offer exceptional electromagnetic absorption and tunable infrared properties. These materials, combined with thermochromic pigments and doped oxides for spectral tuning, enable adaptive camouflage that blends with changing environments.

progetti.titolo: Strategic Autonomous Logistic Uncrewed Battlefield tRiage Intervention System
progetti.obiettivo:
The SALUBRIS project aims at bridging a critical gap in battlefield medical support by designing and validating an ecosystem of Robot Autonomous Systems (RAS) for for casualty triage and evacuation (CASEVAC) in Large-Scale Combat Operations (LSCO), including CBRN-contaminated and denied environments.
The project focuses on multimodal CASEVAC, employing a mix of UxVs in different domains (land, sea, air) to perform casualty detection, recovery, and evacuation, through swarm coordination across the domains.
Furthermore, the project employs sensors data fusion from available sources, including both wearable and nearable sensors, to provide autonomous triage based on the START methodology, employing explainable AI techniques to prioritize the casualties. 
To validate the technologies, the consortium has obtained the support of the Italian Army to host a wargaming exercise involving the SALUBRIS technologies.
The SALUBRIS consortium includes 18 partners and 1 subcontractor from 9 countries, including LE companies providing the backbone for autonomous vehicles and CBRN sensors, SMEs providing advanced technologies and system integration, and leading RTOs providing research capabilities and biomedical expertise.
SALUBRIS contributes to the European defence by delivering a scalable and ethically grounded solution for  next-generation battlefield medical logistics, enhancing survivability, reducing medic exposure, and enabling rapid response in contested operational theatres.

progetti.titolo: Digital Architecture Framework for SoS Readiness and Digital Twin Integration
progetti.bando: Multi-Disciplinary design and Analysis Framework for Aerial Systems
progetti.obiettivo:
The DART (Digital Architecture Framework for System-of-Systems Readiness and Digital Twin Integration) project proposes a transformative approach to the development and lifecycle management of European air combat Systems of Systems in response to the increasing complexity of modern operational environments. It addresses the need for a coherent digital backbone capable of supporting interoperable, data-driven engineering processes across multinational programmes, particularly in the domain of aerial systems and their integration into complex systems of systems.
At its core, DART aims to replace traditional linear development cycles with a continuous model–analyse–build paradigm, enabled by the combined use of Digital Twins and Model-Based Systems Engineering. This approach allows the seamless integration of virtual models with real-world operational data, creating dynamic and continuously evolving digital representations of Systems of Systems that can support decision-making throughout the entire lifecycle, from concept and design to operation, maintenance, and retirement. The project is designed to enhance the consistency, responsiveness, and efficiency of engineering activities, while also enabling a more collaborative and standardised framework across European stakeholders.
The main objective of DART is to establish a scalable and interoperable Digital Twin framework at System-of-Systems level, capable of connecting individual system digital twins into a unified and coherent architecture. This framework supports collaborative engineering and operational optimisation across organisations and nations, while preserving data sovereignty and intellectual property. By leveraging standardised modelling approaches, such as MBSE aligned with recognised frameworks, and by integrating advanced simulation and analytical capabilities, the project enables the exploration of complex operational scenarios and the assessment of design and mission trade-offs in a structured and efficient manner.
From a technical perspective, DART introduces a federated and modular architecture that combines virtual environments, real data integration, and artificial intelligence–driven simulations. This architecture supports secure and standardised data exchange, high-fidelity modelling, and continuous feedback loops between virtual and real domains, enabling predictive analysis and improved system performance. The framework is designed to be scalable and vendor-neutral, ensuring compatibility with existing and future systems, and facilitating interoperability across European and allied defence ecosystems.
The project will be implemented over a period of 36 months through a structured set of activities focused on study and design. Its development follows an iterative approach, with successive cycles leading to progressively refined results and demonstrations. Key outputs include the definition of a Digital Twin framework for defence SoS, a modelling and simulation methodology for SoS engineering, a technological demonstrator of the Digital Twin architecture, and a set of validated proof-of-concept scenarios illustrating its operational value. In addition, the project will deliver a roadmap for the adoption of these concepts within the European Defence Technological and Industrial Base.
To demonstrate its operational relevance, DART focuses on three representative use cases covering different lifecycle stages: collaborative combat and mission-level coordination, sustainment and maintenance optimisation of ISR drones, and lifecycle management of weapon systems. These demonstrators illustrate how Digital Twin technologies can support improved interoperability, predictive capabilities, and lifecycle efficiency in realistic defence scenarios.
Overall, DART is expected to significantly enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of European defence system development by reducing time-to-market, lowering lifecycle costs, and enabling more informed and agile decis

progetti.titolo: A Hybrid Autonomous Unmanned Vehicle system opening new horizons in conducting military operations in the marine environment
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
Recently, there is a growing interest in developing Hybrid Autonomous Unmanned Vehicles (HAUVs) that are capable of air-water trans-media continuous and uninterrupted motion and performance.

The main idea of PASITHEA project is to develop a new design combining the well-known UAV’s and UUV’s technologies into a multi-technology Hybrid Unmanned Vehicle, which can fly, hover in the air and sail, hover under the water, whilst having the ability to repeat air/water trans-media transitions.

The HAUV will be able to be launched and recovered from platforms/units operated and controlled by land, sea (surface/underwater) and air. The project includes the design of a high-level control, command, communication, and intelligence (C3I) system. The carrier vessel/unit can also be embedded with point-to-multipoint networking through the HAUV, meaning that after it releases the HAUV, the system can communicate and relay data with friendly forces operating nearby.

The drone will be designed to return to the operator or to an indicated/preset position either manually, autonomously or combined using an advanced mission planning subsystem. The fact that it is released from underwater means it could will not necessarily be expendable, but recoverable from the underwater mother carrier.

The idea of the projected was based on the fact that recent naval operations in various areas were carried out successfully in a joint environment in which much useful information was generated by unmanned aerial and underwater vehicles. Through these experiences, operators have gained insight into the nature of more complex threats and how they are dealt with to assure successful and effective military operations. Furthermore, vital coast-line infrastructures, as well as inland infrastructures must be defended against threats—some “asymmetric” and some sophisticated—which can be either marine or aerial in nature. These threats are often characterized by their mobility and may be attempted over extended periods of time. Thus, surveillance must take place over wide areas and operate over long time periods, which can have increased risks and wearing/fatigue for the personnel involved. The possible costs and risks involved make strong arguments for the expanded use of unmanned vehicles in modern operations.

Attracted by the prospect of lower unit cost and risk of unmanned vehicles compared to manned vehicles, all the Services have been actively using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), unmanned combat air vehicles (UCAVs), unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs), unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), and unmanned undersea vehicles (UUVs). Based on the operational results, it has become widely suggested that unmanned vehicle systems can be assigned for many operational tasks. Since the operational capability and military worth of unmanned vehicles has been demonstrated in recent military operations, it is essential to exploit and develop on existing capabilities. It is deemed important to develop critical autonomous vehicle-related technologies that are considered essential to the accomplishment of future multidiscipline naval missions.

The concept of the PASITHEA application and the derived relevant technologies have not been combinedly applied in the European defence sector previously. The PASITHEA concept has the potential not only to significantly alter the way that defence forces operate, but to potentially be applied in other domains as well.

The project aims to provide the operators with a strategic advantage, enhancing military multidiscipline operations. In this respect, different application scenarios / concepts can be envisaged.
However, technical challenges where research is needed to develop the envisaged system must be faced.

progetti.titolo: Tactical Drones in Rain and Icing Conditions
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
Class I UAVs are crucial in modern military operations, enhancing armed forces' capabilities in Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition, Reconnaissance (ISTAR), and Search and Rescue (SAR) missions. They also serve as force multipliers, offering immediate air support to ground troops. The Ukraine conflict illustrates the significance of Tactical Drones in Rain and Icing Conditions (TDRIC). This conflict underscores that drones have a pivotal role in contemporary warfare, demanding attention from military entities to accomplish their battlefield goals. Therefore, armed forces' UAVs must consistently perform as intended, maintaining high operational availability.
TDRIC's objectives are:
1)	 Determine and quantify these effects, delivering crucial insights to European armed forces for mission planning and situational awareness enhancement.
2)	Develop rain and icing resilient UAVs, integrating advanced detection and protection technology to significantly boost operational capabilities beyond current standards. 
3)	Advance ground-based climatic testing capabilities and establish standardized procedures for Class I UAV investigations. In summary, TDRIC seeks to enhance the performance and reliability of Class I UAVs in challenging weather conditions, benefiting modern military operations.

progetti.titolo: Wearable device for monitoring warfighter health and sustainability
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo: WEMOR project targets studying the feasibility of a holistic health and wellness management system through a single wearable biomarker monitor device to maximize soldier effectiveness, readiness, protection and recovery. By optimizing humans as a capability, providing the means for human performance enhancement and expanding emergency treatment during combat the project will design the appropriate system for the complete continuum of health monitoring for military personnel.

progetti.titolo: Efficient Autonomous multirole drone Guard for criticaL infrastructures surveillancE missionS
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
Russia's high-intensity war in Ukraine has made the European Union countries aware of hybrid attacks and the tactical importance of drone swarms for both offensive and defensive purposes. For the emergency management and military operational capabilities of EU nations, the complete real-time awareness of the scenario is crucial to increase mission effectiveness and enable risk mitigation actions. In this context, unmanned platforms can be the best option thanks to the absence of a pilot that makes them “expendables” in harsh environments (i.e., nuclear plant disaster, large fire events) or war scenarios.
The intrinsic limitations of convenient small and cheap solutions, like the reduced autonomy and the poor capability in terms of data transmission and computational power can drastically reduce the attractiveness for missions requiring the ground stations being very far from the target location (i.e., nuclear plant disaster or heavy combat scenarios). These weaknesses can be overcome by implementing a sort of “unmanned flying bridge” able to operate as a communication bridge between the small drones flying over the target and the ground station, carrying and releasing the swarm of drones in a location close to the target to maximize the efficiency of the mission by exploiting the whole mini-drones’ autonomy, coordinating the swarm in an automatic or semi-automatic way.
The goal of the EAGLES project is to fill the current design and technological gaps, by performing studies and conceptual design activities on the “flying bridge“ and by studying technologies that will facilitate the development of a System of Systems, nowadays not present on the market, that will give EU defence actors the capability of collecting data and gain information for prompt and effective decision making at low costs and reduced risk.
More in details, EAGLES will focus on the development of communication technologies for both hardware and software, artificial intelligence techniques to manage the mini-drone swarm and to process data acquired by mission sensors, and autonomous flight techniques to assure the drop and rendezvous of mini-drones.

progetti.titolo: Ensuring Circularity of Soldier Personal Protection Equipment
progetti.bando: Non-thematic research actions by SMEs and research organisations
progetti.obiettivo:
UTILE project aims at developing and demonstrating several technologies that allow the implementation of circular strategies to 
recover and reuse of different soldier personal protection equipment (SPE) used by the different European national armies. 
These technologies will be clustered into three, 
i) Digital tools that allow the tracking of materials flows in the supply chain and to support in the stakeholders of the value chain in 
taking the proper decision. 
ii) Technologies that let the upcycling of current SPE products (mechanical and chemical recycling) exploring also new uses of the 
materials recovered for different application in the defence sector. 
iii) Technologies that help to reduce the environmental impact during the manufacturing process by fostering the use of more 
ecofriendly processes and sustainability by replacing petrol based materials by biobased ones. 
UTILE innovations have high disruptive potential: bio-based resins for recyclable fibre composites, novel aramid fibre carding and 
spinning processes for recycled yarn production, innovative UHMWPE defibration, filament production and 3D printing technologies, 
novel pre-preg production employing bio-based resin and recycled aramid fibres. These will be demonstrated in 3 case studies. 
In parallel to this technological and material innovations, UTILE is developing a digital platform including artificial intelligence (AI)-
based Decision Support Systems (DSS) and blockchain technologies for traceability, as well as circularity, environmental and costbenefit analysis (CBA) considerations in order to provide a holistic circular approach at EU level to the SPE value chain. The aim of the 
platform (named EU-level Circular Management System, EUCMS) is to foster the development, implementation, demonstration and 
validation of circularity concepts, first to the SPE value chain, but with the potential and intention to be transferred to other value 
chains in the Defense market.

progetti.titolo: EDIRPA Funding Proposal for Common Armoured Vehicle System (CAVS) Programme
progetti.bando: Common procurement of platforms and replacement of legacy systems
progetti.obiettivo:
Common Armoured Vehicle System (CAVS) Programme is a multinational program for development, procurement and life cycle management of modern armoured 6x6 vehicle system. The programme is led by Finland, who acts as a procurement agent and coordinator. The other Participant Member States are Latvia, Sweden and Germany.

The CAVS Programme is a comprehensive cooperation programme regarding the selected vehicle platform. The programme is based on similar capability needs between the Participant Member States, which generates foundation for further and in-depth cooperation and added value. This similarity is the backbone of the all contracts and decision-making in the CAVS Programme -cooperation. The CAVS Programme covers the whole life cycle of a military product including all necessary support systems and elements. 

Total value of the common procurements in the context of the actions in this proposal is 5 350 031 809,00 €. This value includes activities started after 24.02.2022 but not completed before the signature of the Grant Award and including all the activities planned in the future by the CAVS Programme Participant Member States. The CAVS Programme enables long term commitments as there are planned deliveries until 2037.  

The CAVS Programme consist of three levels covering the whole lifecycle of the vehicles: multinational cooperation under Technical Arrangement, industrial cooperation under joint frame agreements and national deliveries under national procurement contracts. The cooperation includes security of supply, and the agreements with the industry include requirements to include multinational cooperation also with local industry. The CAVS Programme has already now given new start to European 6x6 armoured wheeled vehicle serial manufacturing and it keeps ramping up the production capability in Europe and strengthening its resilience by including great number of SMEs into the supply chain. The Programme is open for new nations with similar needs.
